items.caption:
Elon is now creating the largest building in human history…

The Terafab.

And I don’t think people realize just how insane this project is.

This is a map of Manhattan.

The Terafab will be 3x bigger than Central Park.

1700 football fields in one single Texas building.

It’s insane.

But the wildest part of this project isn’t even the size of the building.

It’s the master plan for why Elon had to build it in the first place.

See Elon went to all the major chip companies and asked to buy out everything they had.

And even if they would have let him, which they didn’t, the total chip supply today is only 2% of what he needs internally for Tesla, SpaceX, Grok, and Optimus.

So the Terafab isn’t really a play to disrupt the current companies…

It’s simply the only way for him to build enough AI chips to keep his projects alive.

What this means…is that when it’s finished….

Elon will own the world’s biggest factory that produces computer chips for all of his companies.

And if it works, it will become the ultimate competitive advantage.

At full capacity, this one building will be able to produce 200 billion AI chips per year.

And most of these will be sent directly into space to build orbital data centers.

So the plan… in summary, is this…

1. Build the biggest building ever created on Earth
2. To produce 50x the existing AI chip supply
3. To send billions of chips into outer space
4. To create floating data centers that power AI for the world

Never bet against Elon.

Follow @kallaway to stay ahead of the curve on tech, AI and robotics

#tech #ai #elonmusk #robotics #technology

Google just released Gemini 4 Argon.

If you’re trying to use AI for complex work tasks, this model offers frontier intelligence to help you get more done.

And it’s especially good at engineering and knowledge work. 

Now, a big reason why Argon is so good at these complex tasks is because it was specifically designed to work with more depth and precision.

This gives it a huge advantage in completing very sophisticated tasks from start to finish without losing any context or reasoning.

Argon is so capable that Google has been using it internally to solve their own problems as well.

A team of Argon agents freed up over 300 terabytes of memory across Google's data centers on their own.

Argon was also able to rewrite 32,000 lines of code in one of Google's video decoders and to make it 2.7 times faster.

So whether it’s your complex tasks or optimizing Google’s own data centers, Argon has just set the new frontier.

If you want to try it out, Gemini 4 Argon is now available for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app.

items.caption:
This company built one of the most advanced AI satellites in the world.

These satellites can detect what model of car is parked in your driveway… from space.

The company behind this is called Planet Labs.

And their Pelican 4 satellites can do something extremely unique.

See, a normal satellite takes a photo and beams the giant file back down to Earth for processing.

But Planet’s satellites have an AI chip on board, so they can read and process photos while still in orbit.

And this gives them some extreme advantages.

For example, they can take a single snapshot of an airport, and identify every single plane on the ground in half a second.

They can collect real-time data on military positioning or even the number are cars in a Walmart parking lot to gauge shopping trends.

But the real innovation is what happens when you link two of these satellites together.

One satellite acts like the wide-angle camera. 

It’s constantly looking at strips of the Earth wider than most cities and re-scans the whole planet, every day.

So it can watch everything simultaneously and detect what changed over time.

Then, it tells the second satellite exactly where to zoom in for detailed viewing.

Together, they’re basically a security system for the entire planet.

And that’s the interesting part…

Imagine using this to track major weather events like hurricanes or wildfires as they develop in real-time.

This is the future of satellite imagery, and in a few years, we’ll have detailed real-time maps of the entire world in seconds.

items.caption:
DoorDash is completely reinventing the food delivery space.

And I don’t think people realize what they’re actually doing under the hood.

Last week they announced a ton of new features at their annual event.

The biggest one, to me, was their ultraquiet food delivery drone, DoorDash Air.

This thing can fly straight from the restaurant to your yard, overtop of all the traffic and dramatically reduces delivery times.

But it turns out, the drone program is only a small piece of their master plan.

I sat down with Stanley Tang, one of the original Co-Founders and Head of Labs at DoorDash.

He was the mastermind behind Air and runs their R&D Labs.

And what he said really surprised me…

The secret sauce at DoorDash isn’t just the drones…it’s the entire delivery operating system layer they’ve built to sit underneath.

DoorDash now has lots of different ways to deliver your food.

They’ve got Dashers, the human drivers, Dot, the autonomous robots, and now Air, the drone fleet.

When an order comes in, they’re able to intelligently route and deliver it in the fastest and most cost efficient way possible.

As they build more and more methods for delivery, including things like drones and other autonomous vehicles, this will increase their ability to serve customers. 

That orchestration layer underneath is the secret sauce behind why they’re so effective.

Stanley also broke down how they’re planning to use AI in their new Text Doordash feature as well as how he runs the R&D Lab to come up with new breakthroughs.

And it’s clear they are doing everything they can to pioneer the future of delivery.

items.caption:
This Japanese broccoli farmer figured out how to automate his farm with AI

His name is Hiroki Tomayasu.

And even though he was never taught how to drive tractors or grow vegetables…

He’s built an entire software system to digitize his farm, all without knowing how to code.

For example…

Hiroki wanted to find a way to automate his fieldwork.

But typically, self-driving tractors like these (https://carbonrobotics.com/carbon-autonomy) are super expensive. 

So instead, he figured out how to build a GPS auto-steer system, that drives his tractor for him, at a fraction of the cost.

He’s also built bots to automate his greenhouse, software for tracking his plant logs,

He’s even using satellite imagery analysis to figure out exactly which crops and fields are performing the best.

And this is all powered by ChatGPT and Codex that he works with every single day.

Hiroki describes using AI like getting access to an ultra-talented engineer that is always by his side.

And the coolest part about this story is that he’s live documenting all of his AI farm experiments on this website (https://note.com/tomiyasu16)

That includes his learnings, what he’s building, and step by step tutorials for other farmers if they want to try it for themselves.

These are my favorite types of AI stories cause it really shows how inventive people can be when they get access to world class tools.

Follow along for more stories like this and shoutout to Hiroki.

items.caption:
OpenAI has officially launched dots.

And this is a massive deal because dots are a completely different category of AI product. 

dots are always-on agents inside of ChatGPT that handle ongoing work.

Each dot has its own cloud computer and browser, which means they can keep working on tasks continuously while you’re away.

Now the big question on everyone’s mind.…is how dots are different from the normal ChatGPT and Codex experiences.

Think of it like this…

ChatGPT and Codex are more reactive.

You ask them questions or give them a task…and they answer to the best of their ability.

So it’s kinda like you’re driving the car and they are the engine. The car doesn’t move unless you push the pedal down.

Dots, on the other hand, are completely different.

They’re designed to be more proactive.

All you have to do is give them an initial objective, set boundaries, and let them cook.

They’ll come back when they need you to weigh in or review important decisions.

So it’s more like you get in the backseat of the car, say where you want to go, and your dot can drive, steer, and fill up its own gas tank.

Now the biggest reason why dots are so compelling, is that they’re powered by GPT-6 Astra.

Essentially, their agent brain is genius level with one of the best models in the world, which means their capacity to do things is extremely advanced.

This is the way most people envisioned working with AI, and it’s now available.

Comment “dots” and I’ll send you more information on how to get yours set up so you can take advantage of the next wave in AI.

items.caption:
DoorDash just officially launched their drone delivery program.

It’s called DoorDash Air.

And this is going to completely change how food gets delivered in the future.

Customers can now place orders that fly straight from the restaurant and land directly in your yard.

Now the big perk is that these drones can fly over top of the traffic, so on average, order flight time is just 5 minutes.

These drones are extremely quiet and you can actually watch the drone’s route via a flyover visualization as it gets delivered.

The service is just starting to roll out in select markets (“in the coming months”) with companies like Chipotle and Popeyes, but this is a peek into the future of cutting edge logistics and delivery.

Now in addition to drones, DoorDash also announced several new AI features that make ordering much more personalized and dynamic.

The biggest one is called Text DoorDash.

This allows you to have a text conversation directly with DoorDash to order your food.

You could say something like, “My mom is in town this weekend. She loves pasta, but doesn’t like seafood. Order us dinner for Saturday night.”

DoorDash now has a personalized AI memory layer that knows exactly where you live and what you like based on past order history, and all the restaurants available to you at that moment.

It can automatically find the perfect meal, list it out for you, and place the order instantly.

This same approach now can be used for ordering groceries and even group dinners…simple text descriptions in, orders ready to go in seconds.

And it all works so well because of the new agentic ordering layer they’re rolling out.

All of this and a bunch of other updates were just announced at their Dash Forward event.

And this is going to completely change the way delivery works in the future.

items.caption:
This factory in China designed robots that build each other

This is the latest project by UBTECH in China and its basically one giant industrial humanoid factory.

This factory in China is building a new robot every ten minutes.

On the floor, humanoid robots load parts and move materials.

Giant robot arms spin to assemble more than two thousand screws into each finished unit.

Automated vehicles and unmanned forklifts haul everything around.

The whole place sits on about two and a half football fields of factory floor.

And it works like a car plant…except the finished products get to walk out when they’re done.

But here’s the wild part…

These particular robots never have to stop working.

Instead of having to charge like most humanoids…

These guys have 2 battery packs in their back.

When one is running low, the robot walks over to the charging station, twists its torso, and pulls the dead battery out of its own back to hotswap.

3 minutes, no human involved.

That means the factory can run 24 hours per day without needing rest or breaks.
I’m telling you, robots building robots used to be something out of a sci-fi movie

Now it’s a literal production line in China with a quota attached.

It seems crazy now, but in a few years, this kind of production will be normalized around the globe

items.caption:
Google Gemini just integrated their agentic capabilities in Gemini Live.

And there’s a way of using this, not many people have tried yet, that is insanely valuable for creators and marketers.

With this integration, you now have voice control over your personal AI agent.

It can access Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Gmail, and even YouTube.

As a creator, I used this new update to build out an entire content pipeline for brand partnerships.

All I had to do was open Gemini Live and verbally describe the workflow I wanted.

And it built this whole thing out for me automatically.

First, it scans my email daily looking for any communication with brands for upcoming partnerships.

When it finds one, it extracts all of the campaign information shared by the brand…and searches all of my best content across Instagram and YouTube to better understand the narratives that have worked well for similar stories in the past.

Then, it uses all that info to automatically build out a new folder in Google Drive and creates a Doc inside it specifically for that campaign with ideas, power phrases, and formats that worked previously.

When I go to make the video, I just open that doc and I already have my notes in there ready to go.

I call this flow data-enabled creativity.

It’s using the data and examples from previous winning videos to help aim my creativity for the new campaign.

Now this is just a single creator workflow.

There are dozens of others you can run.

For example, I asked Gemini to build out an invoice tracking pipeline to keep track of any brand partnerships payments.

I also built an idea repurposer that consistently scans my Google Drive for old script documents and notes that can be repurposed into new content.

And the reason these are so easy to build is because of the voice capabilities in Gemini Live.

This flow is now available for Pro and Ultra users.

Comment “Gemini” and I’ll send through all the links for how to set all of this up.
